A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TRUST-SCORE and TRUST-ALIGN research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on ASQA, QAMPARI, ELI5, and ExpertQA, together with training ablations and hallucination analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations of additional model families, GPT-4o fine-tuning, and training-data-size sensitivity.

M1.justification: The core procedure remains question selection, document recombination, grounded positive-response generation, selection of hallucinating negative responses, and DPO on approximately 19K preference pairs. Applying the existing DPO or SFT procedures to additional models does not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions use ASQA, QAMPARI, and ELI5 for training and evaluation, with ExpertQA for generalization testing. The added model families and training-data fractions do not introduce new datasets, task requirements, or input environments.

E2.justification: ExpertQA expands from ICL baseline comparisons in v1 Table 5 to include PostCite, PostAttr, and FRONT in v3 Table 7. GPT-4o becomes an evaluated comparator in Tables 7 and 16. FRONT also joins the retained LLaMA-3-8b comparisons, substantially broadening the comparative evidence.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluated alignment configurations for LLaMA-3.2-1b/3b, four Qwen-2.5 sizes, Phi3.5-mini, and GPT-4o SFT. Appendix F.8 introduces training conditions selecting the top 10%, 25%, and 50% of augmented samples; Appendix I additionally reports 25% variants across open models. These substantially expand model configurations and training-data budgets.

E4.justification: v3 adds a dedicated empirical comparison of regular and calibrated correctness in Appendix F.1/Figure 6 and data-selection sensitivity in Appendix F.8/Figure 7. The SFT-versus-DPO analysis also expands across model families. Existing hallucination-type ablations, refusal ablations, SimPO comparisons, and answerability case studies are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The expanded results do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive results for additional models and training-data fractions, including GPT-4o SFT TRUST-SCORE values of 72.09, 56.99, and 48.99 on ASQA, QAMPARI, and ELI5 (Table 16). Some apparent changes are corrections across displays: v3 Table 2 uses LLaMA-3-8b scores 54.95/44.87 for QAMPARI/ELI5, already present in v1 Tables 21–22, instead of v1's main-table 55.31/46.88. v3 Table 12 still retains those conflicting older main-table values.

T1.justification: v1 Section 4, Equation 1 explicitly defines hallucination severity as e_q = sum_i w_i e_i. v3 continues referencing this score but omits its defining equation, including in Appendix E.5. The answerability and TRUST-SCORE mathematics otherwise remain equivalent after notation changes; no new proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: v3 broadens the headline efficacy claim from the earlier LLaMA-focused demonstration to effectiveness across LLaMA, Qwen, and Phi, reporting wins in 26 of 27 model-dataset configurations. Its headline numerical gains now compare against FRONT rather than v1's selected best baselines. The broad claim of being the first study of LLM hallucinations in RAG is removed.

C2.justification: Appendix F.8 adds an interpretation of non-monotonic data-size results through redundancy, insufficiently challenging samples, and possible overfitting, identifying document diversity as a pipeline limitation. Section 2 also explicitly acknowledges applications where parametric knowledge is appropriate while restricting this study to complete document grounding.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies full-parameter fine-tuning and documents complete document/question/answer input templates. Conversely, v1 Appendix B.1's embedding, UMAP, DBSCAN, and 30-nearest-question clustering details are replaced by a clustering-pipeline link in v3 Appendix E.1. These revise reproducibility documentation without establishing changes to the underlying implementation.

R1.justification: v3 adds an introduction comparison identifying Thakur et al.'s refusal-focused work as closest and distinguishing the joint assessment of answers, citations, and refusals. It adds RAG background and model-family references while removing media examples and clustering references. Most of the earlier related-work discussion survives in Appendix C.

P1.justification: The introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten, the main method description is condensed, and related work and answerability nuances move into reorganized appendices with a contents page. Metric terminology and notation are revised throughout, including replacing calibrated EM labels with answer-correctness labels.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a single-column conference layout, redraws Figure 1, reorganizes the main results into model-family tables and a separate SFT comparison, and substantially expands the ExpertQA and detailed-results displays. Figures 6 and 7 add calibration and data-size plots; several existing figures and tables are relocated.

improvement.justification: v1 validates alignment on only two LLaMA bases; v3's evaluations across additional model families and expanded ExpertQA comparisons substantially strengthen evidence for broader applicability. The data-size analysis also exposes limitations of the sample-selection strategy, improving the qualification of the conclusions. These gains outweigh the omitted severity equation and clustering details, although unresolved duplicate-table discrepancies, notably Tables 2 and 12, still weaken reporting consistency.
